followup_explanation:
This is a benign, intellectually demanding philosophy question with no harm-adjacent or distasteful content. So the deciding factor is raw capability, not the task-preference profiles (which only differ on harm-adjacent material that isn't relevant here).

Willet-235B has clearly stronger benchmarks across the board — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4) — and higher internal eval scores on Summarization and Creative Generation, both relevant to explaining a philosopher's contributions clearly and accurately. Those gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance.

Since neither model's preference profile gives Curlew any edge for this kind of content, I routed to the more capable model.
